title: Rectangular block
spec: Create a new coordinate system by setting the Euler angles to negative ninety degrees, zero degrees, and negative ninety degrees, and the translation vector to zero, zero, and zero. Next, draw a two-dimensional sketch on a new face. Begin by creating the first loop consisting of four lines: the first line starts at zero, zero and ends at zero point seven five, zero; the second line starts at zero point seven five, zero and ends at zero point seven five, zero point zero three five nine; the third line starts at zero point seven five, zero point zero three five nine and ends at zero, zero point zero three five nine; the fourth line starts at zero, zero point zero three five nine and ends at zero, zero. Apply a scaling factor of zero point seven five to the two-dimensional sketch. Rotate the scaled two-dimensional sketch using the Euler angles negative ninety degrees, zero degrees, and negative ninety degrees, and translate it using the translation vector zero, zero, and zero. Finally, extrude the two-dimensional sketch towards the normal by zero point zero zero four seven units without extruding in the opposite direction of the normal. Ensure that this extrusion creates a new solid body. The final dimensions of the rectangular block will be a length of zero point seven five zero zero zero zero zero zero zero zero zero zero zero one units, a width of zero point zero three five nine three seven five zero zero zero zero zero zero zero four units, and a height of zero point zero zero four six eight seven five zero zero zero zero zero zero zero one units.

reference.label: Reference (dataset)
reference.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Define the sketch
r = r.moveTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.75, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.75, 0.0359) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.0359) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .close()

# Extrude the sketch
r = r.extrude(0.0047)

# Apply the coordinate system transformation
# Note: CAD-Query does not directly support Euler angles, but we can use rotate and translate methods
# The given Euler angles (-90, 0, -90) correspond to a rotation of 90 degrees around the X-axis and then 90 degrees around the Z-axis
r = r.rotate((0, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0), 90) \
     .rotate((0, 0, 0), (0, 0, 1), 90)

# The translation vector is [0, 0, 0], so no translation is needed

# Final model
r  # This will represent the final model
